Why useful for inferring expressibility: Provides basic size information for comparing candidates and planning expected yield/recovery. Length alone is not a strong predictor.
Helps anticipate net charge at the expression or purification pH. Solubility can decrease near the pI, depending on surface properties and buffer conditions.
Can influence colloidal stability, nonspecific interactions and solubility; charge alone does not guarantee good expression.
Unusual compositional biases or high hydrophobic/aromatic content may signal solubility or folding challenges. Cysteine content is relevant to disulfide formation.
A global average hydrophobicity measure. Higher positive values can indicate greater hydrophobic character; local patches may matter even when GRAVY is low.
Highlights contiguous hydrophobic regions that may promote self-association, nonspecific interactions or aggregation.
Exposed hydrophobic residues can promote intermolecular association and aggregation even if overall hydrophobicity is moderate.
Provides a sequence-based estimate of solubility and may highlight regions contributing to poor solubility. Useful for ranking candidates, not as a definitive yield prediction.
Uses spatial arrangement and solvent exposure of residues to identify potential solubility liabilities not apparent from sequence averages.
Identifies sequence segments or structural regions that may nucleate aggregation; especially useful when candidates have similar global solubility scores.
Tool(s): AGGRESCAN3D for structures; CamSol; sequence-based aggregation predictors

Why useful for inferring expressibility: A heuristic based on dipeptide composition that may flag sequence-derived stability concerns. It is not a direct measurement of folding stability, half-life or bacterial yield.
A rough descriptor historically associated with thermostability in globular proteins; limited standalone predictive value for binder expression.
Affects hydrophobic packing and binding, but excessive exposed aromatic surface may contribute to aggregation. Interpret with structure and binding-site context.
Relevant to disulfide formation, native folding and mispairing. The expression compartment matters because the standard bacterial cytoplasm is reducing.
Unexpected loss of the intended fold, excessive disorder or exposed beta-strand edges may indicate folding or aggregation risks. Overall percentages alone are not definitive.
Quantifies solvent exposure and helps identify exposed hydrophobic residues or poorly packed regions that may contribute to aggregation or instability.
Low-confidence loops or disordered regions may indicate flexibility or uncertain folding, but low model confidence is not itself proof of poor expression.
Repetitive or compositionally biased regions may affect solubility, degradation or nonspecific interactions; use as a supporting descriptor.
Tool(s): peptides.py sequence statistics; SEG or equivalent

Why useful for inferring expressibility: Does not predict expressibility, but supports accurate concentration measurement of purified protein and fair yield comparisons across candidates.
